title: Insurance
intro: Each role play has 20 spoken lines or fewer, alternating between Officer or Agent and Client. Pairs read it once, swap roles, then replay it from the coaching notes only. Names, amounts, limits and timeframes are illustrative. Insurers are deliberately left unnamed so no real company's terms are implied; trainers can set a scene at Sri Lanka Insurance, Ceylinco, AIA, Union Assurance, Allianz, HNB Assurance or Softlogic Life without changing the content.
models: A warm greeting and a little rapport before business
Empathy that names the situation: “Five weeks without your car is a long time”
Plain explanations of insurance words: excess, lapse, surrender, non-disclosure
Numbers that add up, written down where it helps
Saying no politely, always with what the officer can do
A clear next step, a reference number, a date, and a proper close

scenarios.title: The direct debit that didn't go through
scenarios.setting: Outbound call from a life insurer's customer care centre, Colombo.
scenarios.characters: Officer: Hasini, customer care officer. Client: Chathura Wickramasinghe, 29, who changed his salary account and forgot to update his direct debit.
scenarios.resolution: Chathura pays within the grace period, so the policy never lapses, and a new direct debit is set up on his new account.

notes.text: Reassure first: “Don't worry, your cover is still active” stops panic before the explanation.
Define the two key words in one line each: lapse (“the cover stops”) and reinstatement (getting it back by paying the arrears).
Two-step teach-back: “What are the two things you'll do today?”

sayThis.say: I can send you the link right now

lines.name: Hasini
lines.text: Good morning, may I speak to Mr. Chathura Wickramasinghe, please? This is Hasini from your life insurer's customer care team.

lines.name: Chathura Wickramasinghe
lines.text: Yes, speaking. Is something wrong?

lines.name: Hasini
lines.text: Nothing serious, but it's important. For security, could you confirm your date of birth?

lines.name: Chathura Wickramasinghe
lines.text: 9th June 1997.

lines.name: Hasini
lines.text: Thank you. Your monthly premium of LKR 6,500 was due on 5th October, but the direct debit didn't go through. The bank returned it.

lines.name: Chathura Wickramasinghe
lines.text: Oh no. I changed my salary account last month. I forgot to tell you.

lines.name: Hasini
lines.text: That explains it. Don't worry, your cover is still active. Your policy has a 30-day grace period, so you have until 4th November to pay.

lines.name: Chathura Wickramasinghe
lines.text: What happens if I miss that date?

lines.name: Hasini
lines.text: Then the policy lapses, which means the cover stops. If anything happened to you, a claim couldn't be paid.

lines.name: Chathura Wickramasinghe
lines.text: That's serious. Can I get it back if that happens?

lines.name: Hasini
lines.text: Usually, yes. That's called reinstatement. You'd pay all the missed premiums, and you may need to fill in a health declaration. It's much easier to pay now.

lines.name: Chathura Wickramasinghe
lines.text: Okay, I'll pay now. How can I do it?

lines.name: Hasini
lines.text: You can pay online by card, or at any of our branches. I can send you a payment link by SMS right now.

lines.name: Chathura Wickramasinghe
lines.text: Please send the link. And what about next month?

lines.name: Hasini
lines.text: I'll email you a new direct debit form for your new account. Once you return it, future premiums will go from there.

lines.name: Chathura Wickramasinghe
lines.text: Got it. Thanks for calling me.

lines.name: Hasini
lines.text: You're welcome. Just to check, what are the two things you'll do today?

lines.name: Chathura Wickramasinghe
lines.text: Pay the 6,500 by the link, and send back the new form.

lines.name: Hasini
lines.text: Exactly. You'll get an SMS receipt. Have a good day, Mr. Wickramasinghe.

scenarios.title: Where is my flood claim?
scenarios.setting: General insurer's call centre. The claim was filed in December 2025.
scenarios.characters: Officer: Kasun, claims call centre agent. Client: Nadeesha Gunawardena, 44, whose house in Kelaniya was flooded during Cyclone Ditwah.
scenarios.resolution: Nadeesha learns her claim is approved, understands the two deductions, gets the missing discharge form and a breakdown, and has a Friday follow-up.

notes.text: Own the gap honestly: “You should have heard from us, and I apologise.”
Explain deductions in plain words: excess is “the part you pay yourself”; age-based valuation is “valued at its age, not new”.
Never pressure a customer to sign a discharge form; offer the breakdown and a review first.

sayThis.say: I'll get back to you on Friday
sayThis.not: I'll revert back to you on Friday.

lines.name: Kasun
lines.text: Good afternoon, thank you for calling. This is Kasun. How can I help you?

lines.name: Nadeesha Gunawardena
lines.text: I made a flood claim for my house in December, after the cyclone. It's almost November now. What's happening?

lines.name: Kasun
lines.text: I'm sorry it's taken so long. Let me check right away. Could you give me your claim number, please?

lines.name: Nadeesha Gunawardena
lines.text: It's HC-25-11873. Nadeesha Gunawardena.

lines.name: Kasun
lines.text: Thank you, Mrs. Gunawardena. The loss adjuster visited your home in January and sent the final report in September.

lines.name: Nadeesha Gunawardena
lines.text: September? Nobody told me.

lines.name: Kasun
lines.text: You should have heard from us, and I apologise. The good news is that the claim has been approved for LKR 1,850,000.

lines.name: Nadeesha Gunawardena
lines.text: Approved? But I claimed 2.4 million.

lines.name: Kasun
lines.text: I understand. The difference is mainly two things. The policy excess, which is the part you pay yourself, is LKR 50,000. And the furniture was valued at its age, not at the price of new furniture.

lines.name: Nadeesha Gunawardena
lines.text: Hmm. So when will I get the money?

lines.name: Kasun
lines.text: We just need the signed discharge form and your bank details. Once we have them, payment takes about ten working days.

lines.name: Nadeesha Gunawardena
lines.text: Nobody sent me any form!

lines.name: Kasun
lines.text: Then I'll email it to you today and post a copy too. Is your email address still the one we have on file?

lines.name: Nadeesha Gunawardena
lines.text: Yes. And if I don't agree with the amount?

lines.name: Kasun
lines.text: You can ask for a breakdown first. I'll attach the loss adjuster's summary to the email. If you still disagree, you can ask us to review it before you sign.

lines.name: Nadeesha Gunawardena
lines.text: Okay, that's fair. Please send both.

lines.name: Kasun
lines.text: I will, within the hour. Your reference for today's call is CC-40921, and I'll get back to you on Friday to check you've received everything.

lines.name: Nadeesha Gunawardena
lines.text: Thank you. At least I know where it is now.

lines.name: Kasun
lines.text: You're welcome, and thank you for your patience. Have a good afternoon.

scenarios.title: Why was my claim rejected?
scenarios.setting: Meeting room at a life insurer's branch, Kandy.
scenarios.characters: Officer: Ruvini, claims officer. Client: Pradeep Dissanayake, 52, whose critical illness claim after heart bypass surgery was rejected by letter.
scenarios.resolution: Pradeep understands why the claim was rejected, keeps his life cover, and leaves with a three-item appeal checklist and the Ombudsman and IRCSL routes.

notes.text: Ask permission before bad news: “May I explain the reason in simple terms?”
Give the reason as facts, not blame: what the form asked, what the records showed, why it matters.
Take the agent concern seriously: IRCSL says it can help where non-disclosure was neither deliberate nor reckless, so it belongs in the appeal.

sayThis.not: I will explain you the reason.

lines.name: Ruvini
lines.text: Good morning, Mr. Dissanayake. Thank you for coming in. How are you feeling after the surgery?

lines.name: Pradeep Dissanayake
lines.text: Better, thank you. But I got this letter saying my claim is rejected. I've paid premiums for three years!

lines.name: Ruvini
lines.text: I'm glad you're recovering, and I understand this letter is a shock. May I explain the reason in simple terms?

lines.name: Pradeep Dissanayake
lines.text: Yes, please. The letter is full of legal words.

lines.name: Ruvini
lines.text: When you applied in 2023, the form asked if you'd ever been treated for diabetes or high blood pressure. The answer given was no.

lines.name: Pradeep Dissanayake
lines.text: Yes, I think so.

lines.name: Ruvini
lines.text: During the claim, the hospital records showed you'd been on diabetes medicine since 2020. Diabetes is a major risk for heart disease, so it affects whether we accept the cover and at what price.

lines.name: Pradeep Dissanayake
lines.text: But the agent filled in the form. He said small things don't matter.

lines.name: Ruvini
lines.text: Thank you for telling me that. It's important, and I'll note it. But the decision is based on the signed form, so the claim can't be paid as it stands.

lines.name: Pradeep Dissanayake
lines.text: So I lose everything? All that money?

lines.name: Ruvini
lines.text: Your basic life cover continues as long as you keep paying. I'll also ask the claims team to consider refunding what you paid for the critical illness cover.

lines.name: Pradeep Dissanayake
lines.text: This isn't fair. Can I do anything?

lines.name: Ruvini
lines.text: Yes, you can appeal. Send us a letter within 30 days with any medical evidence and your concern about the agent. A senior panel who weren't part of the first decision will review it.

lines.name: Pradeep Dissanayake
lines.text: And if they say no again?

lines.name: Ruvini
lines.text: Then you can write to the Insurance Ombudsman or complain to the IRCSL, the insurance regulator. Both are free. The details are on the back of this letter.

lines.name: Pradeep Dissanayake
lines.text: Okay. I'll write the appeal. Can you help me with what to include?

lines.name: Ruvini
lines.text: Of course. I'll write down three things: your letter, your doctor's report, and what the agent told you. Is there anything you'd like me to explain again?

lines.name: Pradeep Dissanayake
lines.text: No, I understand now. Thank you for being honest.

lines.name: Ruvini
lines.text: You're welcome. Take care of your health, Mr. Dissanayake. We'll reply to your appeal in writing.

scenarios.title: Five weeks at the garage
scenarios.segment: Delayed motor claim and assessor dispute
scenarios.setting: Motor claims desk at a general insurer's branch, Kurunegala.
scenarios.characters: Officer: Amila, motor claims officer. Client: Lahiru Fonseka, 31, whose eight-year-old Toyota Aqua was hit from behind. The garage quoted LKR 420,000; the assessor approved LKR 285,000.
scenarios.resolution: The agreed amount is released so repairs start today, the disputed bumper gets a joint re-inspection on Thursday, and Lahiru has a decision date and the policy clause.

notes.text: Make the numbers add up: 65,000 + 60,000 + 10,000 explains the full LKR 135,000 gap.
Split agreed from disputed: pay what isn't in question now, and review only the part that is.
Admit your side of a delay plainly, without blaming the garage or the customer.

sayThis.not: It is there in the policy.

lines.name: Amila
lines.text: Good morning, Mr. Fonseka. I'm Amila from motor claims. How can I help?

lines.name: Lahiru Fonseka
lines.text: My car has been at the garage for five weeks! The garage says you approved only 285,000, but the repair is 420,000.

lines.name: Amila
lines.text: Five weeks without your car is a long time. I'm sorry. Let me go through the assessor's report with you.

lines.name: Lahiru Fonseka
lines.text: Please. I don't understand why they cut so much.

lines.name: Amila
lines.text: There are three differences. First, the garage wants a new rear bumper, but the assessor says it can be repaired. That's about LKR 65,000.

lines.name: Lahiru Fonseka
lines.text: But the bumper is cracked!

lines.name: Amila
lines.text: That's a fair point, and I'll come back to it. Second, the car is eight years old, so new parts have a 20% deduction for age. That's about LKR 60,000. Third, your policy excess is LKR 10,000.

lines.name: Lahiru Fonseka
lines.text: Nobody explained any of this. And why did it take five weeks?

lines.name: Amila
lines.text: Part of the delay was waiting for the garage's final estimate, and part was on our side. The report waited a week for approval. I apologise for that.

lines.name: Lahiru Fonseka
lines.text: So what now? I need my car for work.

lines.name: Amila
lines.text: Here's what I suggest. We release the LKR 285,000 today so the garage can start work. Then a senior assessor will inspect the bumper with the garage on Thursday.

lines.name: Lahiru Fonseka
lines.text: And if he agrees it needs replacing?

lines.name: Amila
lines.text: Then we'll pay the extra for the bumper, less the age deduction. You'll have our decision by Monday.

lines.name: Lahiru Fonseka
lines.text: Okay. But the age deduction, is that fair?

lines.name: Amila
lines.text: It's written in your policy, so I can't remove it. I'll email you the page so you can see it yourself.

lines.name: Lahiru Fonseka
lines.text: Fine. When will I get the car?

lines.name: Amila
lines.text: The garage says about five working days once work starts. I'll call you on Monday with the bumper decision.

lines.name: Lahiru Fonseka
lines.text: Alright. Thank you for explaining properly.

lines.name: Amila
lines.text: You're welcome. Your claim number is MC-77310 if you need us. Have a good day.

scenarios.title: The bill at discharge
scenarios.setting: Insurer's help desk at a private hospital in Colombo, on discharge day.
scenarios.characters: Officer: Shehani, insurer's hospital desk officer. Client: Ayesha Marikar, 36, going home after four nights of treatment for dengue.
scenarios.resolution: Ayesha is discharged on time, understands the LKR 46,000 shortfall, and has a review form for the room charge she wasn't warned about.

notes.text: Start with what is covered (“most of the bill”) before what isn't, so the customer hears the good news first.
Let the customer do the sum (“So 40,000 plus 6,000”): it confirms understanding without a test.
Say no and open a door: the room limit stands, but the missing warning at admission is grounds for a review.

lines.name: Shehani
lines.text: Good morning, Ms. Marikar. I'm Shehani from your insurer's hospital desk. I hope you're feeling better.

lines.name: Ayesha Marikar
lines.text: Much better, thanks. But the cashier says I have to pay 46,000. I thought insurance covers everything!

lines.name: Shehani
lines.text: I understand, that's a surprise on discharge day. Let me show you the bill and go through each part.

lines.name: Ayesha Marikar
lines.text: Okay.

lines.name: Shehani
lines.text: Your total bill is LKR 312,000. Your policy pays for the treatment, tests and medicines in full. That's most of the bill.

lines.name: Ayesha Marikar
lines.text: Then why do I pay anything?

lines.name: Shehani
lines.text: There are two parts. First, your policy covers a room up to LKR 15,000 a night. You stayed in a LKR 25,000 room for four nights, so the difference is LKR 40,000.

lines.name: Ayesha Marikar
lines.text: Nobody at admission told me about a room limit!

lines.name: Shehani
lines.text: I'm sorry you weren't told. That should be explained at admission, and I'll report it today. Second, there's LKR 6,000 for items the policy doesn't cover, like toiletries and phone calls.

lines.name: Shehani
lines.text: Exactly, LKR 46,000. We pay the other LKR 266,000 directly to the hospital, so you don't need to claim it back.

lines.name: Ayesha Marikar
lines.text: Can't you make an exception? I was very sick.

lines.name: Shehani
lines.text: I'm afraid I can't change the room limit. But because you weren't told at admission, you can ask us to review the room charge. I'll give you the form.

lines.name: Ayesha Marikar
lines.text: Yes, please. Will that delay my discharge?

lines.name: Shehani
lines.text: Not at all. You can go home today. The review happens separately, and we'll reply in writing.

lines.name: Ayesha Marikar
lines.text: Okay. I'll pay the 46,000 now.

lines.name: Shehani
lines.text: Thank you. Here's a printed summary of what we paid and what you paid. Next time, please ask for a room within your limit at admission.

lines.name: Ayesha Marikar
lines.text: I will. Thanks for explaining it clearly.

lines.name: Shehani
lines.text: You're welcome. Take care, and get plenty of rest.

scenarios.title: Three months and still no maturity payment
scenarios.setting: Phone call to a life insurer's head office complaints unit, Colombo.
scenarios.characters: Officer: Dilshan, complaints officer. Client: Rohan Peiris, 58, whose LKR 1,200,000 endowment policy matured in July and still hasn't been paid.
scenarios.resolution: The complaint is logged and escalated, the cause (a closed bank account) is found, Rohan knows the next step and the outside routes, and a Monday call is promised.

notes.text: Name the failure and own it: “That's our mistake, and I apologise.” No hiding behind the branch.
Give a complaint number, a written confirmation and a date, so the complaint is tracked, not just heard.
Explain outside routes accurately: the Ombudsman is free and needs only a signed letter, and the customer should choose either the Ombudsman or the IRCSL.

sayThis.not: I'll put a complaint for you.

lines.name: Dilshan
lines.text: Good morning, Complaints Unit, this is Dilshan. How can I help you?

lines.name: Rohan Peiris
lines.text: I want to make a formal complaint. My policy matured in July. It's almost November, and I still haven't got my 1.2 million. I've written to the branch twice.

lines.name: Dilshan
lines.text: I'm very sorry, Mr. Peiris. Three months is far too long, especially after two letters. I'll log this as a formal complaint now. May I have your policy number?

lines.name: Dilshan
lines.text: Thank you. The maturity was approved in July, but the payment is on hold. The bank account on file was closed, so the transfer came back.

lines.name: Rohan Peiris
lines.text: Nobody told me that! I gave my new account details at the branch in August.

lines.name: Dilshan
lines.text: Then that's our mistake, and I apologise. Your August letter isn't in the system. I'm escalating this to the Head of Claims today.

lines.name: Rohan Peiris
lines.text: What does that mean for me? When will I get the money?

lines.name: Dilshan
lines.text: Your complaint number is CMP-26-1457, and you'll get written confirmation by email today. Our policy is a full written reply within 14 days, but I'm pushing for payment within five working days.

lines.name: Rohan Peiris
lines.text: And if it doesn't happen?

lines.name: Dilshan
lines.text: Then you can take it outside the company. You can write to the Insurance Ombudsman. It's free, and you only need a signed letter with your policy number and the complaint.

lines.name: Rohan Peiris
lines.text: Or the IRCSL?

lines.name: Dilshan
lines.text: Yes, you can also complain to the IRCSL, the insurance regulator. But choose one. The Ombudsman won't take a case the IRCSL has already investigated.

lines.name: Rohan Peiris
lines.text: Okay. I hope I don't need either.

lines.name: Dilshan
lines.text: I hope so too. To make the payment, could you email a copy of your new passbook page or a bank statement?

lines.name: Rohan Peiris
lines.text: Yes, I'll send it this afternoon.

lines.name: Dilshan
lines.text: Thank you. As soon as it arrives, I'll take it to the Head of Claims myself. I'll call you on Monday with a payment date.

lines.name: Rohan Peiris
lines.text: Thank you. This is the first time someone has given me a straight answer.

lines.name: Dilshan
lines.text: I'm sorry it took this long. Thank you for your patience, Mr. Peiris. Speak to you on Monday.

scenarios.title: “The agent promised me 15%”
scenarios.characters: Officer: Chamari, branch customer relations manager. Client: Sanduni Jayasekara, 25, a software QA engineer who has paid LKR 10,000 a month for two years.
scenarios.resolution: Sanduni gets a plain explanation of what was promised versus what she bought, a formal mis-selling complaint is opened, and she leaves with written options and no pressure to decide.

notes.text: Explain the product before judging the sale; let the documents, not the officer's opinion, show the gap.
Be accurate even when it helps the agent: the tax point was broadly right, the guarantee was not.
Don't defend the agent and don't trash them: “The company is responsible for what its agents say” keeps it professional.

lines.name: Chamari
lines.text: Good afternoon, Ms. Jayasekara. Please have a seat. I understand you have a concern about your policy.

lines.name: Sanduni Jayasekara
lines.text: Yes. The agent told me this was an investment with a guaranteed 15% a year. I've paid 240,000, but the statement says I'd get only 140,000 if I take it out!

lines.name: Chamari
lines.text: I can see why you're upset, and thank you for bringing it to us. Could I see the statement and your proposal documents?

lines.name: Sanduni Jayasekara
lines.text: Here. He also said I could take my money out any time, and that it's tax-free.

lines.name: Chamari
lines.text: Let me explain how this policy actually works, and then we'll look at what the agent said. Is that okay?

lines.name: Sanduni Jayasekara
lines.text: Okay.

lines.name: Chamari
lines.text: Part of each premium pays for your life cover and the policy charges, which are higher in the first years. The rest is invested. The return depends on the fund, so it isn't guaranteed. Here it's shown as a projection only.

lines.name: Sanduni Jayasekara
lines.text: So 15% was never guaranteed?

lines.name: Chamari
lines.text: Not according to these documents. And taking money out in the early years means a surrender charge, which is why the value is low now.

lines.name: Sanduni Jayasekara
lines.text: And the tax-free part? Was that a lie too?

lines.name: Chamari
lines.text: That part is broadly right. Under this year's tax change, payouts on death, maturity or surrender aren't taxed for individuals. But there's no tax relief on the premiums you pay.

lines.name: Sanduni Jayasekara
lines.text: I feel cheated. Can I cancel and get everything back?

lines.name: Chamari
lines.text: The 21-day cooling-off period, when you could cancel for a full refund, has passed. But what you've told me about the guarantee is serious, so I'm logging a formal complaint about how the policy was sold.

lines.name: Sanduni Jayasekara
lines.text: What will that do?

lines.name: Chamari
lines.text: We'll review the sale, including the agent's notes and anything he gave you in writing. The company is responsible for what its agents say. You'll get a written answer, and if you're not satisfied, you can go to the Insurance Ombudsman or the IRCSL.

lines.name: Sanduni Jayasekara
lines.text: And what should I do with the policy now?

lines.name: Chamari
lines.text: Please don't decide today. Each choice has a cost, so I'll give you a written comparison: continue, reduce the premium, or stop. Take it home and think it over.

lines.name: Sanduni Jayasekara
lines.text: Okay. Do you need anything else from me?

lines.name: Chamari
lines.text: If you have any messages or notes from the agent, please send copies. Your complaint number is MS-2210, and I'll update you within a week.

lines.name: Sanduni Jayasekara
lines.text: I have his WhatsApp messages. I'll send them tonight. Thank you for being honest with me.

scenarios.title: I can't afford the premium anymore
scenarios.setting: Agent's evening visit to the customer's home, Matara.
scenarios.characters: Agent: Saman, life insurance agent. Client: Nimal Senanayake, 46, a three-wheeler driver who has paid LKR 8,000 a month for four years on LKR 2 million of cover.
scenarios.resolution: Instead of surrendering at a LKR 174,000 loss, Nimal halves his premium and keeps LKR 1 million of cover for his family.

notes.text: Thank the customer for raising hardship early; it keeps the door open for next time.
Show the cost of surrender in rupees, then give the options one at a time, with numbers.
Respect the decision: an agent who doesn't push builds trust, and IRCSL lists financial difficulty as a main reason behind refund requests.

sayThis.say: Your premium drops to about LKR 4,000
sayThis.not: The premium will come to around 4,000 like that.

lines.name: Saman
lines.text: Good evening, Mr. Senanayake. Thanks for letting me come by. You mentioned on the phone that you want to stop your policy?

lines.name: Nimal Senanayake
lines.text: Yes. Fuel is expensive, hires are down, and my daughter is starting A/L tuition. I can't pay 8,000 a month anymore.

lines.name: Saman
lines.text: That sounds really hard, and I'm glad you told me before missing a payment. Can I show you all the options before you decide?

lines.name: Nimal Senanayake
lines.text: Okay, but I need the money.

lines.name: Saman
lines.text: Of course. If you surrender now, you'd get about LKR 210,000. You've paid LKR 384,000, so you'd lose about 174,000, and your family would have no cover.

lines.name: Nimal Senanayake
lines.text: That much loss? I didn't know.

lines.name: Saman
lines.text: That's why I want you to see the other choices. One: we reduce your cover from 2 million to 1 million. Your premium drops to about LKR 4,000 a month.

lines.name: Nimal Senanayake
lines.text: Four thousand I can manage. What else?

lines.name: Saman
lines.text: Two: you stop paying and make the policy paid-up. You keep a smaller cover with no more premiums, but you get no cash now.

lines.name: Nimal Senanayake
lines.text: But I need some cash for the tuition.

lines.name: Saman
lines.text: Three: a policy loan. You could borrow up to about LKR 150,000 against the policy. There's interest, and anything not repaid comes out of the final payout.

lines.name: Nimal Senanayake
lines.text: A loan sounds risky for me. I'll take the smaller premium.

lines.name: Saman
lines.text: That's your decision, and it makes sense. Just to check, can you tell me what changes?

lines.name: Nimal Senanayake
lines.text: I pay 4,000 a month, and if something happens to me, my family gets 1 million, not 2.

lines.name: Saman
lines.text: Exactly. I'll bring the change form tomorrow for you to sign. The new premium starts next month.

lines.name: Nimal Senanayake
lines.text: Thank you. I thought you'd try to stop me.

lines.name: Saman
lines.text: I just want you to choose with all the facts. If things get better, we can look at increasing the cover again.

lines.name: Nimal Senanayake
lines.text: That's good to know. Thank you, Saman.

lines.name: Saman
lines.text: You're welcome. See you tomorrow at the same time.

scenarios.title: A widow's first claim
scenarios.setting: Agent's home visit, Galle, three weeks after the funeral.
scenarios.characters: Agent: Ishan, life insurance agent. Client: Kanthi Abeysekara, 61, whose husband Sunil died of a heart attack. She is the nominee and has never handled the family's papers.
scenarios.resolution: The claim form is completed together, the missing policy document won't block it, and Kanthi has a timeline, weekly updates and written steps in two languages.

notes.text: A personal condolence, then permission and pace: “we'll go slowly”; offer a family member.
Remove the blockers before they worry her: a missing policy document has a simple fix.
Commit to a rhythm of updates (“every Friday”), not just “we'll let you know”.

sayThis.say: I'm so sorry about your husband

lines.name: Ishan
lines.text: Good morning, Mrs. Abeysekara. I'm so sorry about your husband. He was always kind to me.

lines.name: Kanthi Abeysekara
lines.text: Thank you, Ishan. I don't know anything about his papers. He did all that.

lines.name: Ishan
lines.text: That's alright. I'm here to help, and we'll go slowly. Would you like your son to join us?

lines.name: Kanthi Abeysekara
lines.text: He's at work. Let's do it now. I want to finish this.

lines.name: Ishan
lines.text: Of course. Mr. Abeysekara had a life policy with us for six years. You're the nominee, so the benefit comes to you. It's LKR 2,000,000.

lines.name: Kanthi Abeysekara
lines.text: Two million? I didn't know it was that much.

lines.name: Ishan
lines.text: Yes, he kept it going every month. To make the claim, I need a few documents. May I tell you what they are?

lines.name: Kanthi Abeysekara
lines.text: Yes, please.

lines.name: Ishan
lines.text: The death certificate, your NIC, the policy document if you can find it, and your bank passbook. I'll fill in the claim form with you.

lines.name: Kanthi Abeysekara
lines.text: I have the death certificate and my NIC. The policy, I'm not sure.

lines.name: Ishan
lines.text: Don't worry. If you can't find it, I'll ask the office for a copy, and you'd just sign a short letter. It won't stop the claim.

lines.name: Kanthi Abeysekara
lines.text: How long will it take? The funeral costs were a lot.

lines.name: Ishan
lines.text: Once we have everything, it usually takes two to three weeks. The policy is more than two years old, so there shouldn't be extra checks.

lines.name: Kanthi Abeysekara
lines.text: That would be a big help.

lines.name: Ishan
lines.text: I'll take copies today and submit them tomorrow morning. I'll call you every Friday until the money is in your account.

lines.name: Kanthi Abeysekara
lines.text: Thank you, son. You're very patient with me.

lines.name: Ishan
lines.text: It's the least I can do. Here's a note with my number and the claim steps in Sinhala and English. Please call me any time.

lines.name: Kanthi Abeysekara
lines.text: I will. Please thank your office for me.

lines.name: Ishan
lines.text: I will. Take care of yourself, Mrs. Abeysekara.

scenarios.title: Why has my medical cover gone up?
scenarios.setting: Branch counter, Batticaloa. The customer's first language is Tamil.
scenarios.characters: Officer: Kavitha, customer service officer who speaks Tamil and English. Client: Sivakami Rajendran, 66, a retired teacher whose medical renewal rose from LKR 48,000 to LKR 62,000.
scenarios.resolution: Sivakami understands why the premium rose, has three costed options in writing in Tamil and English, and time to decide with her son before 30th November.

notes.text: Offer the customer's language first; mixing English with Tamil key words is fine if it helps.
Grade the English: short sentences, “One… Two…” signposts, and numbers written down.
Give the downside of the cheapest option honestly, then hand the decision back: “It's your choice.”

lines.name: Kavitha
lines.text: Good morning, madam. Please have a seat. How can I help you today?

lines.name: Sivakami Rajendran
lines.text: Morning. This letter... insurance price going up. 48,000, now 62,000. Why?

lines.name: Kavitha
lines.text: I see. I can explain slowly in English, or in Tamil. Which is easier for you?

lines.name: Sivakami Rajendran
lines.text: English slowly. Tamil words also, if hard.

lines.name: Kavitha
lines.text: Of course. There are two reasons. One: you are now 66. At 66, you move to a new age group, and the price is higher.

lines.name: Sivakami Rajendran
lines.text: Age... okay. And two?

lines.name: Kavitha
lines.text: Two: hospital costs in Sri Lanka go up every year. Medicines and tests cost more. So the price is higher for everyone.

lines.name: Sivakami Rajendran
lines.text: My pension is small. 62,000 is too much.

lines.name: Kavitha
lines.text: I understand. Let me show you three choices. I'll write the numbers for you.

lines.name: Sivakami Rajendran
lines.text: Yes, write, please.

lines.name: Kavitha
lines.text: Choice one: same cover, LKR 62,000. Choice two: a lower hospital limit, 300,000 instead of 500,000, for LKR 51,000. Choice three: same cover, but you pay the first LKR 20,000 of each hospital bill, for LKR 45,000.

lines.name: Sivakami Rajendran
lines.text: The first 20,000 myself? Hmm. I go to hospital maybe one time a year.

lines.name: Kavitha
lines.text: Then choice three may save money, but each time you go into hospital, you pay 20,000 first. Choice two is in the middle. It's your choice.

lines.name: Sivakami Rajendran
lines.text: Can I ask my son? He is in Colombo.

lines.name: Kavitha
lines.text: Of course. You have until 30th November to decide, and your cover continues until then. Here's the paper in Tamil and English.

lines.name: Sivakami Rajendran
lines.text: Thank you. Very kind.

lines.name: Kavitha
lines.text: Just to check, what's the last date?

lines.name: Sivakami Rajendran
lines.text: 30th November.

lines.name: Kavitha
lines.text: That's right. Call me or come in any time. Here's my number. Have a good day, madam.
